documents.title: The ADOIT Forms User Manual
documents.summary: ADOIT Forms is an extension of the ADOIT EAM suite enabling users to design, manage, and complete forms via a graphical interface without programming, facilitating data capture, updates, valuations, and proposals.
documents.content:
User Manual

Welcome to the ADOIT Forms user manual!

ADOIT Forms is powered by the leading EAM suite ADOIT. It enables you to design, manage and complete forms for ADOIT with an easy to use graphical user interface.

Your added values:
• Design Forms simply. Without programming.
• Capture ADOIT data intuitively. Without training and workshops.
• Periodically ensure that ADOIT data is up to date.
• Obtain ad-hoc valuations.
• Propose new objects.
• And more!

For the installation process of ADOIT Forms, refer to the Installation Manual and the Hardware and Software Requirements.

Check the What's new section to see new features introduced with the latest version.

children.title: About this Manual
children.summary: This manual provides instructions on how to use ADOIT Forms features.
children.content: In the following documentation you will find instructions on how to use the features of ADOIT Forms as a

children.title: Template Designer
children.summary: The Template Designer section explains how to create and manage form templates.
children.content: • Templates: Learn how to design and manage Templates.

children.title: Forms Submitter
children.summary: The Forms Submitter section guides users on accessing and completing forms to update ADOIT objects and proposing new objects.
children.content:
• My Forms: Learn how to access and complete your Forms to update your ADOIT objects.
• Proposals: Learn how to propose new ADOIT objects.

children.title: Forms Reviewer
children.summary: The Forms Reviewer section covers reviewing submitted forms, available from ADOIT version 18.0 onwards.
children.content: • Review submissions: Learn how to review submitted Forms (available for ADOIT version 18.0 or newer).

children.title: Learn more
children.summary: Additional resources include the Installation Manual, Hardware and Software Requirements, BOC EAM Marketplace, and BOC Group Resources.
children.content:
For additional information, take a look at:
• ADOIT Forms Installation Manual
• ADOIT Forms Hardware and Software Requirements
• BOC EAM Marketplace
• BOC Group Ressources

children.title: Design a template
children.summary: ADOIT Forms enables designing questionnaire templates via a GUI requiring user permissions and OAuth connection to ADOIT, facilitating efficient object updates.
children.content:
ADOIT Forms allows you to design questionnaire templates for ADOIT with an easy to use graphical user interface.

note

The details on how to connect to your ADOIT installation are described in the OAuth section.

note

You need to need to have user permissions to be able to open the templates component of ADOIT Forms.

Enable your colleagues to modify existing objects in ADOIT efficiently and keep information up to date.

children.title: How to design a new update template
children.summary: To design a new update template, select the repository, ensure 'Update templates' tab is active, and create a new template.
children.content: Go to Templates, select the repository where the template should be stored, ensure that the tab Update templates is selected and open New template.

children.title: Template attributes
children.summary: Template attributes include title, optional description, object type, target language, form recipient, template owner, approval requirement, and approver(s); approval requires ADOIT v18+.
children.content:
First, you have to fill out the following fields for the template:
1. Title: Choose a descriptive name for the template.
2. Description (optional): Add a description that describes what the template is about.
3. Object type: Select the ADOIT object type that is used for this template.
4. Target language: Per default, the ADOIT primary database language is selected for all templates. Select a language, if you want another ADOIT content language to be updated by Forms of this template.
5. Form recipient: Select from which responsibility relation the Form responsibilities should be derived.
6. Template owner: The selected user is displayed on Templates overview page.
7. Approval required: Decide whether the object should be updated directly after the form submission, or whether it requires approval.
8. Approver: Select user(s) that will receive an email notification for every submitted Form and will be responsible for reviewing them (only when approval is required).

note

The approval feature is available for ADOIT version 18.0 or newer.

children.title: Question attributes
children.summary: Question attributes define question title, optional description, linked ADOIT property or relation, relation target type, and optional relation target selection restrictions; saving is required.
children.content:
Once the template attributes are defined, you can Add Question and define for each question:
1. Question title: Define an easy-to-understand question.
2. Question description (optional): Add some context to the question.
3. Property: Select an ADOIT attribute or an ADOIT relation of the previously choosen object type.
4. Relation target: For property values of type relation, it is additionally necessary to define a target object type.
5. Restrict relation target selection: For property values of type relation, it is possible to select a saved ADOIT search query to limit the selectable target objects for this question.

note

Do not forget to save your template before closing the template designer!

children.title: How to assign an update template and distribute Forms
children.summary: Assign update templates by selecting objects via Explorer or saved queries, then distribute forms which send email notifications; reminders can be sent for open forms.
children.content:
Go to Templates, then Select a repository and open Distribute for a selected Template.

You can choose out of all the visible objects of the Object type that is defined for this Template by:
• Explorer: Select a single or several objects directly in the object explorer.
• Saved search query: Select a public saved ADOIT search query that contains objects of the respective object type.

After clicking Distribute forms are created for all selected objects. Email notifications to responsible users are sent (after users confirmation) on activation of a template or on distribution when a template is active.

A reminder can be sent to all responsible users for forms with status Open.

children.title: How to manage an update template
children.summary: Manage update templates by viewing distributed forms with statuses (Open, Updated, Approved) and last completion dates; only Open forms can be edited if approval is required.
children.content:
Go to Templates and open Distribute for a selected template.

Under Distributed Forms you can see all created Forms that belong to this template.

Status shows the current state of each Form: Open (not yet submitted) or Updated (submitted). When approval is required, Approved is shown after the Form has been reviewed and approved. Note, that forms requiring approval can be opened only if status is Open.

Last completion date shows when the Form has been submitted the last time. If there is no date visible, the Form has not been completed yet.

children.title: How to edit an update template
children.summary: Edit update templates by opening and saving changes; existing forms based on the template update immediately.
children.content:
Go to Templates and open Edit for a selected template. After you have made your changes, confirm them with Save.

note

Existing Forms based on this template are updated directly!

children.title: How to import sample update templates
children.summary: Import best practice update templates into a selected repository for immediate use and distribution; deleted or renamed templates can be re-imported.
children.content:
Go to Templates, select the repository where the template should be imported and click Import best practice templates.

The imported templates can directly be used and distributed.

After an imported template is deleted or the name is changed, the template can be imported again.

Enable your colleagues to suggest new objects for ADOIT.

children.title: How to design a new proposal template
children.summary: Design new proposal templates by selecting repository, switching to 'Proposal templates' tab, and creating a new template.
children.content: Go to Templates, select the repository where the template should be stored, switch to the tab Proposal templates and click New template.

children.title: Template attributes
children.summary: Proposal template attributes include title, optional description, object type, target language, target repository and folder, template owner, approval requirement, and approver(s); approval requires ADOIT v18+.
children.content:
First, you have to fill out the following fields for the template:
1. Title: Choose a descriptive name for the template.
2. Description (optional): Add a description that describes what the template is about.
3. Object type: Select what kind of ADOIT objects should be created with this template.
4. Target language: Per default, the ADOIT primary database language is selected for all templates. Select a language, if you want another ADOIT content language to be updated by this template.
5. Target repository: Select the ADOIT respository, where the new objects should be created.
6. Target folder: Select the ADOIT object folder, where the new objects should be created.
7. Template owner: The selected user will receive an email notification for every created object (only when approval is not required).
8. Approval required: Decide whether the object should be created directly after the form submission, or whether it requires approval.
9. Approver: Select user(s) that will receive an email notification for every proposal and will be responsible for reviewing them (only when approval is required).

note

The approval feature is available for ADOIT version 18.0 or newer.

children.title: Question attributes
children.summary: Proposal question attributes mirror update templates: question title, optional description, linked ADOIT property or relation, relation target type, and optional selection restrictions; saving is necessary.
children.content:
Once the template attributes are defined, you can Add Question and define for each question:
1. Question title: Define an easy-to-understand question.
2. Question description (optional): Add some context to the question.
3. Property: Select an ADOIT attribute or an ADOIT relation of the previously choosen object type.
4. Relation target: For property values of type relation, it is additionally necessary to define a target object type.
5. Restrict relation target selection: For property values of type relation, it is possible to select a saved ADOIT search query to limit the selectable target objects for this question.

note

Do not forget to save your template before closing the template designer!

children.title: How to activate a proposal template
children.summary: Proposal templates are inactive by default; activate them in the Templates view under 'Proposal templates' tab to make them available in the Proposals view.
children.content:
Proposal templates are deactivated per default. Only activated proposal templates are availeble in the Proposals view.

To activate a proposal template, go to the Templates view, select the repository where the template is stored, switch to the tab Proposal templates and click Activate in the template row you want to activate.

children.title: How to edit a proposal template
children.summary: Edit proposal templates by selecting and saving changes in the Templates view under 'Proposal templates' tab.
children.content: Go to the Templates view, select the repository where the template is stored, switch to the tab Proposal templates and open Edit for a selected template. After you have made your changes, confirm them with Save.

children.title: How to import sample proposal templates
children.summary: Import best practice proposal templates for immediate checking and activation; deleted or renamed templates can be re-imported.
children.content:
Go to the Templates view, select the repository where the template is stored, switch to the tab Proposal templates and click Import best practice templates.

The imported templates can directly be checked and activated.

After an imported template is deleted, or the name is changed, the template can be imported again.

children.title: Submit a Form
children.summary: ADOIT Forms allows users to update existing ADOIT objects like Application Components or Business Objects via forms.
children.content: ADOIT Forms enables you to easily update your ADOIT objects, like Application Components or Business Objects.

children.title: How to access a Form
children.summary: Access forms via direct email notification links or through the My Forms view on ADOIT Forms website; OAuth connection details are in the OAuth section.
children.content:
You can access Forms you are responsible for by
1. Opening a Form directly out of an ADOIT Forms email notification
2. Opening My Forms on ADOIT Forms (boc-cloud.com)

note

The details on how to connect to your ADOIT installation are described in the OAuth section.

children.title: Email notifications
children.summary: Email notifications contain direct deep-links to forms for responsible users to open them in a web browser.
children.content: Every email notification sent by ADOIT Forms contains one or more direct links to a Form you are responsible for. By clicking on such a link, the Form is opened in your web browser.

children.title: My Forms
children.summary: My Forms view lists all forms assigned to the user, showing form name (clickable), template used, and status (Open, Updated, Approved).
children.content:
In this view you can see a list of all Forms your ADOIT user is responsible for.
• Name: Click on the name of the Form to open the respective Form in a new browser tab.
• Template: Template that is used for this Form.
• Status: Shows the current state of the Form: Open (not yet submitted) or Updated (submitted). When approval is required, Approved is shown after the Form has been reviewed and approved. Note, that forms requiring approval can be opened only if status is Open.

children.title: How to complete a Form
children.summary: Complete forms by answering mandatory and optional questions; submit to update objects directly or send for approval if required; forms can be reopened and resubmitted anytime.
children.content:
A Form consists of a set of questions. Every question is of a specific question type like free text, dropdown, date or references. Mandatory questions are marked with a red *.

Within a Form you can click on the name and open the underlying object directly in ADOIT.

After you have updated all questions, the Form can be submitted by clicking on Submit. After the changes are saved, a success report is displayed and the Form status changes to Updated. Note that in case approval is not required, the object is updated directly in the repository. Otherwise, the Form is sent to the review.

note

The approval feature is available for ADOIT version 18.0 or newer.

note

The selected ADOIT Forms user interface language may differ from the ADOIT data language, which depends on the template settings.

You can come back to the Form and submit again any time.

children.title: Propose a new object
children.summary: Users can propose new ADOIT objects via proposal forms; OAuth connection details are provided in the OAuth section.
children.content:
ADOIT Forms enables you to easily propose new objects for your ADOIT, like a new Application Component or a System Software, by using proposal Forms.

note

The details on how to connect to your ADOIT installation are described in the OAuth section.

children.title: How to access proposal Forms
children.summary: Access proposal forms via the Proposals view on ADOIT Forms website, listing accessible proposal forms with names and descriptions.
children.content:
You can access proposal Forms by opening the Proposals view at ADOIT Forms (boc-cloud.com)

note

The Proposals view is only available, if there is at least one proposal Form accessbile for your user.

In this view you can see a list of all proposals Forms your ADOIT user has access to.
• Name: Click on the name to open the proposal Form.
• Description: Details of the proposal Form.

children.title: How to complete a proposal Form
children.summary: Complete proposal forms by answering questions including a unique object name; submit to create objects directly or send for approval; UI language may differ from ADOIT data language.
children.content:
A Form consists of a set of questions. Every question is of a specific question type like free text, dropdown, date or references. Mandatory questions are marked with a red *.

note

You must enter an unique name for the object you are proposing. If an object with the same name already exists, the proposal cannot be completed successfully.

After you have updated all questions, the Form can be submitted by clicking on Submit. After the changes are saved, a success report is displayed. Note that in case approval is not required, a new object is created directly in the repository. Otherwise, it is sent to the review.

note

The approval feature is available for ADOIT version 18.0 or newer.

note

The selected ADOIT Forms user interface language may differ from the ADOIT data language, which depends on the template settings.

children.title: Review submissions
children.summary: Forms Reviewers can approve or reject submitted forms when approval is required; this feature requires ADOIT v18+ and appropriate permissions.
children.content:
In case approval is required, Forms Reviewers can see an overview of submitted forms and approve or reject them.

note

The approval feature is available for ADOIT version 18.0 or newer.

note

You need to have user permissions to be able to open the approval component of ADOIT Forms.

children.title: Review a single proposal
children.summary: Review single proposals by modifying submitted values, then approve or reject with optional rejection reasons sent via email to submitters.
children.content:
Select a proposal and review values submitted in a form.

It can be rejected (in that case submitted values are lost) or approved. Once it is approved, a new object is created in the repository and a success message is displayed. Note, that values can be modified before approval.

Data can be modified and directly approved or changes can be saved and approved (or rejected) at another time.

On both rejection and approval, an email is sent to the submitter of the proposal.

When rejecting a proposal, a confirmation dialog is displayed. You can optionally enter a rejection reason. If provided, the reason is included in the rejection email sent to the person who submitted the proposal.

children.title: Review a single update form
children.summary: Review single update forms by modifying submitted values, then approve or reject with optional rejection reasons emailed to submitters.
children.content:
Select an update form and review values submitted.

It can be rejected (in that case submitted values are lost) or approved. Once it is approved, the changes are applied to the object in the repository and a success message is displayed. Note, that values can be modified before approval.

On both rejection and approval, an email is sent to the submitter of the Form.

When rejecting an update form, a confirmation dialog is displayed. You can optionally enter a rejection reason. If provided, the reason is included in the rejection email sent to the person who submitted the form.

children.title: Personalized access with OAuth 2.0
children.summary: ADOIT Forms uses OAuth 2.0 to grant personalized access to ADOIT content, respecting existing user permissions without granting extra rights.
children.content:
This section describes how you can grant ADOIT Forms personalized access to your ADOIT contents with the technology OAuth 2.0.

note

You can only access and change ADOIT contents that your ADOIT user is permitted to. No additional access rights to ADOIT contents are granted by ADOIT Forms.

children.title: User prerequisites
children.summary: User prerequisites include having a personal ADOIT user with assigned ADOIT Forms license, at least one user group, and repository; system role assignment is optional.
children.content:
• You must have a personal ADOIT user (in the User Management of ADOIT Administration Toolkit)
• The ADOIT user needs to have an ADOIT Forms license seat assigned
• The ADOIT user needs to have at least one user group assigned
• The ADOIT user needs to have at least one repository assigned
• An assigned system role is not mandatory

children.title: Security and comfort improvements
children.summary: From version 1.7.0, security and comfort improvements include recommending SSO, marking ADOIT Forms as a First-party application in ADOIT Administration, and setup instructions for OAuth 2.0 connections.
children.content:
Starting from version 1.7.0 of ADOIT Forms, additional security and comfort improvements are introduced (for ADOIT version 18.1.0 and higher).
• To avoid having to provide ADOIT credentials, it is strongly recommended to use ADOIT with SSO.
• To avoid having to explicitly approve the connection (see 2. Allow access below), the ADOIT Forms should be marked as a First-party application in the ADOIT Administration.
• For ADOIT instances connected after this change was implemented, ADOIT Forms is automatically marked as a First-party application by the setup script (see Installation).
• For ADOIT instances connected before this change was implemented, it might be required to set it up. Go to ADOIT Administration and open Authentication and OAuth 2.0 To set is up, the option First-party application should be enabled for the connection with the ID forms-boc-cia. OAuth 2.0 configuration is described here.

Connecting ADOIT version below 18.1.0 or without proper configuration described above, establishing the connection is more explicit as described below.

children.title: OAuth flow - establish a connection
children.summary: OAuth flow requires users to explicitly allow ADOIT Forms to access their ADOIT account.
children.content: You have to allow ADOIT Forms to use your ADOIT user by the following steps.

children.title: 1. Login
children.summary: Login step involves verifying the correct ADOIT instance URL and clicking Connect in the dialog.
children.content:
Whenever you see the Connect dialog, please check if the correct ADOIT instance URL is visible and click on Connect.

note

Before you click on Connect, verify that this is an actual ADOIT URL of your organisation!

children.title: 2. Allow access
children.summary: Allow access step requires clicking Allow after login to connect ADOIT Forms to the ADOIT account; successful connection is shown on start page.
children.content:
After the successful login, please click Allow to connect ADOIT Forms to your ADOIT account.

If your user is eligible for the connection, you will see the currently connected ADOIT instance on the ADOIT Forms start page.

children.title: Terminate access
children.summary: Terminate access by clicking logout in ADOIT Forms or revoking access in ADOIT user interface under Applications.
children.content:
Just click on the red logout button on the top right corner.

Alternatively, you can revoke access in your ADOIT user interface in the user menu under Applications.

children.title: Message: Access denied!
children.summary: Access denied message appears if user explicitly denies access or has an active session in ADOIT Administration.
children.content:
This message is displayed in two cases:
1. User clicked explicitly on Deny
2. User has an active session in ADOIT Administration

children.title: Architecture
children.summary: Architecture includes ADOIT instance (on-premise/cloud), ADOIT Forms client-side (browser), server-side (AWS), ADOIT web client, BOC Cloud Services, web browser, OAuth 2.0, and REST API components.
children.content:
ADOIT instance | ADOIT instance which is deployed either on premise, in a private cloud or at BOC cloud services.
ADOIT Forms (client-side) | The part of ADOIT Forms that is executed directly in the web browser of the user.
ADOIT Forms (server-side) | The part of ADOIT Forms that is executed on Amazon Web Services (AWS). The URL https://adoit-forms.boc-cloud.com/ must be accessible from the user's web browser. No ADOIT data is stored or processed on server-side.
ADOIT web client | ADOIT running in the web browser of the user.
BOC Cloud Services | Cloud-native application services provided by BOC and hosted on AWS.
Web browser | Web client used to access both ADOIT instance and ADOIT Forms by the user.
OAuth | OAuth 2.0 component provided by ADOIT.
REST API | RESTful endpoints provided by ADOIT.

children.title: Software Requirements
children.summary: Software requirements: ADOIT Enterprise Edition 17.1+, recommended browsers are Microsoft Edge and Google Chrome.
children.content:
Requirements
ADOIT | Enterprise Edition: ADOIT 17.1 or higher
Recommended Browser | Microsoft Edge Google Chrome

children.title: ADOIT Setup
children.summary: ADOIT setup requires enabling REST API with OAuth 2.0, CORS, SSL/HTTPS, licensed RESTful services, assigning system roles and user rights for ADOIT Forms, and proper user license and permissions; see Installation Manual for details.
children.content:
This section describes the setup requirements for ADOIT when using ADOIT Forms.
Requirements
Authentication | To read and write data from and to ADOIT instances, the REST API with OAuth 2.0 must be enabled. To ensure ease of use, it is strongly recommended to use ADOIT with SSO. See relevant section.
CORS policy | CORS has to be enabled.
Security | SSL/HTTPS is required.
RESTful services | Licensed and activated.
System Settings (Modules) | ADO Forms has to be assigned to the system roles using ADOIT Forms.
User Rights Management | All user and access rights for ADOIT Forms are defined in the ADOIT Administration. NOTE: Only content that the user has write access to, can be updated by the user via ADOIT Forms.
User License | To enable an ADOIT user to access ADOIT Forms, an ADOIT Forms user license has to be assigend to the respective user.
Template Designer | To grant an ADOIT user template designer rights, the user must have an ADOIT Forms license, Forms Designer user group and FormsDesigner system role assigned.
Forms Submitter | To grant an ADOIT user Forms submitter rights, the user must have an ADOIT Forms license assigned and at minimum read access to the root folder objects.
Forms Reviewer (available for ADOIT version 18.0 or newer) | To review submitted Forms, the user must have an ADOIT Forms license, Forms Designer user group and FormsDesigner system role assigned.
Base URL | Compliant with connection settings.

For more information on the setup process, please check the Installation Manual document.

children.title: Hardware Requirements
children.summary: Hardware requirements depend on ADOIT's needs and may require increased resources depending on ADOIT Forms usage.
children.content:
Make sure the requirements of ADOIT are met.

Depending on the usage scenario of ADOIT Forms, it might be required to increase the hardware resources for ADOIT.

children.title: Installation
children.summary: Installation involves preparing the ADOIT instance for ADOIT Forms and granting user access.
children.content:
This section describes how to
1. prepare your ADOIT instance to be used with ADOIT Forms.
2. grant ADOIT user access to ADOIT Forms.

children.title: 1. Activate ADOIT Forms
children.summary: Activate ADOIT Forms in ADOIT Administration by enabling RESTful services, OAuth 2.0 with specific APIs, whitelisting CORS domains, creating system roles and user groups; requires environment restart and compliant Base URL.
children.content:
In your ADOIT Administration open Settings, go to ADOIT Forms and General.

Setup enables ADOIT Forms and leads to the following changes in the ADOIT settings:
• Activation of the setting Activate standard RESTful Services globally
• Activation of the setting Activate OAuth 2.0 with the
• Repository scenarios: Repository read APIs, Repository write APIs, Repository search APIs
• User scenarios: User read APIs
• Metamodel scenarios: Metamodel read APIs
• Activation of Allow whitelisted CORS for both General and REST (See Configure CORS for more details) Domains to be whitelisted are:
• https://adoit-forms.boc-cloud.com
• Activation of OAuth 2.0 and creation of an client
• Creation of the system role FormsDesigner
• Creation of the user group Forms Designer

note

The Base URL set for the ADOIT (see related instruction) must be compliant with the URL provided in the connection setup. A common source of issues is that it is different (for example a test URL provided in a production environment) or additional endings like /auth.view, /main.view, etc. are added.

note

Changing this setting requires a restart of the ADOIT environment.

children.title: 2. Configure users for ADOIT Forms
children.summary: Configure users for ADOIT Forms by assigning user groups, system roles, licenses, and ensuring appropriate access rights for Template Designers, Forms Submitters (update/proposal), and Forms Reviewers.
children.content:
In your ADOIT Administration you can enable your ADOIT users to use ADOIT Forms as
• Template Designer
• Forms Submitter (update)
• Forms Submitter (proposal)
ADOIT Forms user type | Needed configuration
Template Designer / Forms Reviewer | 1. Assign user group Forms Designer. 2. Ensure that system role FormsDesigner is assigned. 3. Only for named use license scenarios: Assign ADOIT Forms scenario under Named user.
Forms Submitter (update) | 1. Ensure write access to relevant Objects. 2. Only for named use license scenarios: Assign ADOIT Forms scenario under Named user. 3. Ensure that in Settings > System settings (Modules) the module ADOIT Forms is assigned to the used custom system role.
Forms Submitter (proposal) | 1. Ensure write access to relevant target folder. 2. Only for named use license scenarios: Assign ADOIT Forms scenario under Named user. 3. Ensure that in Settings > System settings (Modules) the module ADOIT Forms is assigned to the used custom system.
Forms Submitter (proposal and update with approval required) | 1. Assign arbitrary system role selected in Settings > ADOIT Forms > Settings for approvals. 2. Only for named use license scenarios: Assign ADOIT Forms scenario under Named user. 3. Ensure that in Settings > System settings (Modules) the module ADOIT Forms is assigned to the used custom system role.

children.title: ADOIT Forms Glossary
children.summary: Glossary defines key terms: ADOIT element/object, Form, Proposal template, Template (update and proposal), emphasizing templates as blueprints linked to ADOIT attributes for specific object types.
children.content:
ADOIT element | A synonyme for ADOIT Object
ADOIT object | An architecture component like a Business Capability, an Application Component or a Data Object that is stored in the ADOIT respository. Can be updated by a Form.
Form | User-friendly forms to update existing ADOIT objects or to propose new ADOIT objects.
Proposal template | A blueprint of a Form to propose new ADOIT objects.
Template | A blueprint of a Form. There are update and proposal templates. A template consists of questions that are linked to ADOIT attributes or relations. A template is always defined for a single ADOIT object type.
Update template | A blueprint of a Form to update data of existing ADOIT objects. Can be used to distribute Forms to object responsibles by assigning the template to selected ADOIT objects.
